clue.text: Gaseous element or a metallic one returning information

indicators.note: returning means both the little word or and the metal that follows it are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
tin is a metallic element
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A chemistry question about whether a gas or a metal brings back data.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a metallic one' reads as describing an element; it is a particular metal, and 'returning' applies to the little word before it as well.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the colourless gas making up most of the air, a chemical element.

clue.text: One trade that's just the job

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a deal is a trade or transaction

explanation.surface: A single line of work that suits someone perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something perfect, just what is wanted, is described as just the job.

clue.text: Type of clothing liable to draw attention

parts.note: liable in the sense inclined or apt, as is ready
to draw a cart is to tow it
to give ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A kind of outfit that tends to get people looking at you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liable to' reads as one phrase but splits: 'liable' is READY and 'to' is a link before the next pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-the-peg garments made in standard sizes are a category of clothing.

clue.text: Titanic — a boat once fantastic

parts.note: a gig is a light ship's boat
antic is an archaic adjective meaning grotesque or fantastic

explanation.surface: The famous ship described as a fantastical old vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics make 'Titanic' look like the liner, but it is just the adjective meaning huge.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic and the answer are both adjectives meaning enormous, of colossal size.

clue.text: Having no position yet

parts.note: no in the sense not
with means having, as in a man with a beard
standing is position or status

explanation.surface: Someone with no status as yet.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in a different order from the clue words: no, having, position.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are used to mean nevertheless or despite that.

clue.text: Gives birth (with assistance) to son

parts.note: help means assistance
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A mother delivers her son with help from a midwife.
explanation.walkthrough: The parenthesis looks like an aside, but every word in it supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Of a dog or similar animal, to produce young is to bring forth a litter.

clue.text: A bit on the side in port

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount, as in not a whit
by means beside or to one side, as in stand by

explanation.surface: A lover kept on the side in some harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit on the side' is an idiom for a lover; here it splits into two pieces. WHITBY is a North Yorkshire fishing port.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yorkshire coastal town is a harbour town, so an example of a port.

clue.text: Some of 21 object

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a part taken from inside the referenced entry

parts.note: the solution to 21 across, the errors to be fixed

explanation.surface: Objecting to part of an earlier entry.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue says 2; the page prints 21, the answer to 21 across, which holds the run.
explanation.definitionFit: An end is an aim or purpose, the object of an action.

clue.text: Frank has the sulks — he goes to court

parts.note: plain means frank or outspoken
a tiff is a fit of peevishness or sulking

explanation.surface: A man called Frank sulks and then sues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name but is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: The party who brings a case before a judge is the one who takes action at law.

clue.text: Grandmother overcome by drink in Malaysian island

indicators.note: overcome by means held down inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a peg is a measure of spirits
nan is an informal word for grandmother

explanation.surface: Granny is drunk on holiday in Malaysia.
explanation.definitionFit: The island off the west coast of the Malay peninsula is part of Malaysia.

clue.text: Abel's position in the field?

parts.note: Abel came after Adam and Cain among men, and in cricket there is a fielding position of that name

explanation.surface: The field where Abel tended his flocks, or a cricket field.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a fielding position is named for its order; Abel, after Adam and Cain, was the next man in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket fielding position on the off side behind the slips bears this name.

clue.text: Perform piano accompaniment to song

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
a lay is a song or ballad

explanation.surface: A pianist accompanies a singer in a recital.
explanation.definitionFit: To play is to perform a piece of music or a role.

clue.text: Bad habit causing anxiety

definitions.meaning: chewing the fingernails, a nervous habit
tense and suspenseful, keeping one on edge

explanation.surface: A nervous habit that itself causes worry.
explanation.definitionFit: The compound names the habit of chewing nails and describes a tense, suspenseful situation.

clue.text: Kiev athlete resolved to become a nun

indicators.note: resolved in the sense broken down and reorganised, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Ukrainian sportswoman decides to enter a convent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' looks like 'determined', but it signals rearranging KIEVATHLETE.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a woman who takes vows in a religious order is said to do this.

clue.text: Villa home is hard to electrify

parts.note: Aston is the Birmingham district that is home to Aston Villa football club
taken as written
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A villa house hard to wire for electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: ASTON is the Birmingham district whose football team is Aston Villa; 'Villa' is not a house.
explanation.definitionFit: To electrify an audience is to thrill or amaze them.

clue.text: Foul outrages outside right, a substitute

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters wrap round the next piece
foul in the sense messed up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: In football, after foul play outrages the crowd, a substitute replaces the outside right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside right' looks like a football position; 'outside' puts SUROGATE (the anagram of OUTRAGES) round R.
explanation.definitionFit: A surrogate is someone or something standing in for another.

clue.text: Join fool in conversation

indicators.note: in conversation means the word is spoken rather than written

parts.note: a nit is a fool, short for nitwit

explanation.surface: An invitation to join an idiot in chatting.
explanation.definitionFit: Broken bones knit, that is they grow together and unite.

clue.text: It's obvious Dad has turned up, and Mum, possibly, as well

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a mother is an example of a parent

explanation.surface: Clearly Dad has arrived, and Mum may have come too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' looks like 'arrived', but it reverses PA to give AP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is clear or plainly seen is obvious; the definition reads as 'it's plain'.

clue.text: Deliver without charge

explanation.surface: Delivery at no cost.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to set at liberty, the other is costing nothing.

clue.text: Court official has to give advice to employees

parts.note: to tip is to give advice or a pointer
staff are the employees

explanation.surface: A court officer must counsel the people who work there.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipstaff is a sheriff's officer or court usher, originally carrying a tipped staff.

clue.text: Slight upset suffered by soldier visiting scene of mutiny

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
the Nore, a Thames estuary anchorage, was the site of the 1797 naval mutiny

explanation.surface: A soldier feels slighted on a visit to where a mutiny took place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight upset' looks like a small disturbance; 'upset' turns GI into IG. The Nore is an anchorage at the mouth of the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: To slight someone is to snub or ignore them.

clue.text: In bullfight, general errors to be fixed

indicators.note: In at the front means the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: a corrida is a Spanish bullfight

explanation.surface: A general at a bullfight makes mistakes that need correcting.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrigenda are errors in a book listed for correction.

clue.text: Pound for a book

definitions.meaning: the American poet Pound's first name
a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A pound paid for a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like money but is the poet Ezra Pound.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the poet Pound's forename and the name of an Old Testament book.

clue.text: Season in state prison

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state
pen is short for penitentiary, a prison

explanation.surface: A time spent locked up in a state jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Season' looks like a noun; here it is the verb, to mature.
explanation.definitionFit: To season timber or cheese is to let it mature or age.

clue.text: Pasta that was just dandy

definitions.meaning: an eighteenth-century fop who affected Continental fashions

explanation.surface: Pasta that was simply fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just dandy' reads as 'excellent', but 'dandy' means a fop, with 'that was just' marking it as a past sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a tubular pasta and also an old name for an affected English fop.

clue.text: Bend where car came to grief

indicators.note: came to grief means wrecked, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written; the run of letters across car came is a coincidence, not the setter's device

explanation.surface: The bend on which a car crashed.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc is a curve, a bent line.

clue.text: Grant immunity to former emperor facing arrest at last

parts.note: ex means former
EMP is an abbreviation for emperor

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word arrest

explanation.surface: A deposed emperor facing arrest is given immunity.
explanation.definitionFit: To exempt someone is to free them from an obligation or liability.

clue.text: Secure after a fashion

indicators.note: after a fashion means arranged differently, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Something is made safe, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of SECURE gives the answer, and the whole clue defines it: saving someone secures them, in a way.
explanation.definitionFit: To save someone from danger is in a sense to make them safe.

clue.text: Given leave, manage to be friendly

definitions.meaning: as in ... with you, go away
to be on good terms with someone

explanation.surface: Someone given time off learns to be sociable.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to depart, to cope, and to be on good terms.
